title: Construct finite and integral supported localization before scalar passage
statement: Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ and a proof $h_\ell$ that $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. Let $t:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Use the records of [def-sf-localization-stage-data]. For every finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, the integral localization record $\mathrm{SfIntegralLocalization}(\ell,E,k,h_\ell,t,i,j)$ is nonempty. This includes its family of finite positive-level records and all conditional quantitative Tor bounds. No rational or algebraically closed localization is asserted.

source.place: Finite/integral part of (1), (2) and (3), and Finite Tor amplitude through Other stages.

proof.text: For each positive level use [lem-sf-positive-finite-localization-construction] and choose its finite localization record F n inside the existence proof. These records include all conditional quantitative finite Tor fields.

Obtain ordinary integral recollement from [lem-sf-integral-ordinary-recollement-realization]. With F and this ordinary recollement apply [lem-sf-integral-localization-comparisons] to get the qualitative integral record C, including closed_pull_reduction.

For each closed or open integral input, [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] gives a product and an actual SfIntegralDirectImage for the recorded tower. The ordinary recollement image comparison identifies its object with the restricted completed image; compose its inverse with the inverse of the corresponding image comparison in C. The ordinary push_reduction property says every actual reduction map of that limit is invertible. This proves closed_limit and open_limit directly. Finite type over k makes X Noetherian, so the open immersion is quasi-compact; both source schemes satisfy the finite-type hypotheses of the direct-image theorem.

For each of the five operations and each n, evaluate its reduction isomorphism at an integral constructible input and apply the full inclusion to obtain the ambient derived isomorphism. Tor amplitude is invariant under an isomorphism: compose each representative isomorphism with its inverse in the defining all-module test. The appropriate finite Tor interval, transported through this isomorphism, is the desired nth integral reduction interval. All finite levels use the same N=2d+c; N≥0 implies a≤b+N and a≤b+N+1. Thus all five integral intervals hold uniformly.

An integral finite-Tor input supplies a,b and one ordered interval at every reduction by definition. Apply the corresponding interval result of step 4 and use the output functor codomain for constructibility. This gives each preservation field. Assemble the original SfIntegralLocalization record with C's comparison fields and the limit fields of step 3, F, and the newly proved Tor fields. No definition, target statement, coefficient category or unit route changes.

proof_origin.place: Finite/integral construction as before; the uniform integral Tor transfer is now proved directly from the actual reduction comparisons, following Other stages.

from.place: Finite/integral part of (1), (2) and (3), and Finite Tor amplitude through Other stages.

lean.statement: theorem sfIntegralLocalizationConstruction (k : Type u) [Field k] (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : IsUnit (l : k)) (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (X : Scheme.{u}) (t : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated t] [LocallyOfFiniteType t] [QuasiCompact t] {Z U : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] (hij : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ) : Nonempty (SfIntegralLocalization l E k hl t i j)
